added_models.model: HCV viral-kinetic mathematical model (Perelson/Dahari lineage) fitted to on-treatment serum HCV RNA decline; later run in real time to set per-patient DAA duration

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: A multiscale viral-kinetic model fitted to Gao 2010 daclatasvir kinetics inferred two modes of action and a 45-min HCV half-life; no prediction compared yet.
efficacy.short: Kinetic model fitted to daclatasvir patients
efficacy.quote: Here, we show that understanding the effects of daclatasvir in vivo requires a multiscale model that incorporates drug effects on the HCV intracellular lifecycle, and we validated this approach with in vitro HCV infection experiments.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 23431163, PMC3593898). The model was fitted to patient data, so it is an opener, not a comparison; the two-mode prediction was validated in vitro, not in patients.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the in-silico track at its first NS5A-class use. Fitting to patient kinetics predicts nothing testable in patients, so untested; the same Dahari/Uprichard/Cotler program later ran the model prospectively (Etzion 2020), which is why the track exists.

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: Fitted after the fact to 58 patients on sofosbuvir + daclatasvir, simeprevir or ledipasvir, the model projected cure by 6-13 weeks for all and flagged the one relapser as under-treated.
efficacy.short: Retrofit projects cure times, flags relapser
efficacy.quote: The modeling suggested that the patient who relapsed would have benefitted from an additional week of sofosbuvir+ledipasvir.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 26907973). The abstract says the analysis was retrospective but not whether fits were blind to SVR; retrodiction stands on the stated design. Canini 2017 (PLoS One, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0187409) repeated the retrofit for daclatasvir + asunaprevir (89/95 cured; 6-8 weeks projected) with no status change.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: 12-week SVR outcomes were known before the model was fitted. It reproduced them (all projected cured within the course; the single sofosbuvir/ledipasvir relapse projected to need one more week), so retro, patient-level. The shortening projections were not tested in these patients.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: model-projected time to cure (<=13 weeks for all 58) vs SVR in 57/58 on 12-week sofosbuvir + daclatasvir/ledipasvir/simeprevir

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: Real-time modeling of week 0-4 kinetics shortened therapy in 11/29 patients on velpatasvir-, elbasvir- or ledipasvir-based regimens; SVR 28/29, the one relapse a 6-week sofosbuvir/velpatasvir patient.
efficacy.quote: Real-time mathematical modeling of early HCV kinetics can be utilized for shortening DAAs duration in approximately 40% of patients without compromising treatment efficacy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 33082372, PMC7575564). Regimens named in the companion paper Dasgupta 2020 (doi:10.1093/infdis/jiaa219): sofosbuvir-velpatasvir, elbasvir-grazoprevir, sofosbuvir-ledipasvir. NCT03603327 has no posted results, so registry_date is the first-posting date. Single-arm pilot, n=29, 11 shortened.
efficacy.judgement: First prospective prediction on this track: the model chose, in real time, which patients could stop early (patient-level). 10/11 shortened patients were cured as predicted; the one relapse was a model-shortened sofosbuvir/velpatasvir patient, so the patient-level call is partial, but the primary endpoint (SVR 97%) held and the source calls it a success. Scored same, not contra, because the prediction was the preserved cure rate, which held; the miss is recorded here.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: SVR 28/29 (97%) overall and 10/11 in model-shortened patients vs the model's prediction of cure at the shortened duration

patient_trials.quote: Treatment duration was shortened in 11 of the 29 patients (38%). SVR was achieved in 28 of the 29 patients (97%).

added_models.model: TK-NOG human-liver chimeric mouse (CIEA) inoculated with patient-derived genotype 1b HCV carrying NS5A L31M + P32del from a ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: TK-NOG humanized-liver mice (Osaka/CIEA, not the Hiroshima uPA/SCID line) were infected with serum from a ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure carrying NS5A-P32del.
efficacy.short: P32del patient virus into TK-NOG mice
efficacy.quote: We inoculated human hepatocyte chimeric mice with sera from a patient with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir therapy failure carrying a genotype 1b HCV with NS5A L31M and P32del or from a DAA-naïve patient carrying wild-type virus.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 30684016). Host strain (TK-NOG) is from the paper's keywords and the CIEA co-author, not from a methods read.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from hcv-chimeric-upa-scid-mouse: a different humanized-liver host (TK-NOG, Osaka/CIEA) carrying a different inoculum (patient-derived P32del virus) and making a different, patient-level prediction (which retreatment a P32del failure can respond to). Osawa 2019 (J Gen Virol) used the Hiroshima uPA/SCID system and belongs on the existing track.

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: Mice carrying the patient's P32del virus stayed viraemic on ledipasvir plus a nucleotide NS5B inhibitor, reproducing the donor's ledipasvir/sofosbuvir relapse, but cleared on simeprevir + nucleotide or interferon.
efficacy.short: P32del mice relapse on ledipasvir, as patient did
efficacy.quote: The virus was resistant to the ledipasvir/GS-558093 (a nucleotide analog inhibitor of NS5B polymerase) regimen but susceptible to either simeprevir plus GS-558093 or peg-interferon alfa-2b, compared to the wild-type virus.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The patient side is the serum donor's own ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure as the paper states it, plus Uemura 2019 (J Gastroenterol, doi:10.1007/s00535-018-01543-9, epub 2019-01-05): 3/3 GLE/PIB retreatment failures carried NS5A-P32del. Both were public before this paper (epub 2019-01-25), so the mouse reproduced a known result.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the inoculum came from a patient who had already failed ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, and P32del failure on NS5A-inhibitor regimens was in print (Uemura 2019) twenty days earlier. The mouse reproduced it, so retro, patient-level. Its forward prediction (NS5A-free two-drug combinations cure P32del) has no patient test I could find; Mawatari 2020 adds one more P32del GLE/PIB failure, consistent but not a test, so no later entry.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: persistent serum HCV RNA on ledipasvir/GS-558093 in P32del mice vs the donor patient's ledipasvir/sofosbuvir relapse

considered_not_added: Shi 2013 humanized-mouse GT2a/2b combination failure vs Sulkowski 2014 (daclatasvir + sofosbuvir 24 weeks, 92% SVR in GT2): same system as the draft's hcv-chimeric-upa-scid-mouse track (Hiroshima uPA/SCID), so it is a second prediction on an existing track, not a new system; not added here.

FDA Harvoni label Oct 2014 section 12.4 (baseline NS5A RAPs, relapse 5/23 vs 2/85): an earlier regulator comparison on the existing hcv-replicon-huh7 track (earlier dating of the 2015 Daklinza entry), not a new system; not added here.

Osawa 2019 J Gen Virol (doi:10.1099/jgv.0.001268): glecaprevir/pibrentasvir vs GT1b RAVs in Hiroshima/PhoenixBio human-hepatocyte chimeric (uPA/SCID) mice, the same system and group as Shi 2013; a patient-level retrodiction that belongs on the existing hcv-chimeric-upa-scid-mouse track, not a new one.

Guedj 2013 PNAS (doi:10.1073/pnas.1203110110): verified to exist (PMID 23431163); a model fitted to Gao 2010 daclatasvir kinetics with in-vitro, not patient, validation, so not a comparison; used only as the untested opener of the in-silico track.

Canini 2017 PLoS One (daclatasvir + asunaprevir retrofit, 89/95 cured) and Dasgupta 2020 J Infect Dis (glecaprevir/pibrentasvir retrofit projecting 4-7 week courses): further retrodictions on the in-silico track with no status change and no shortened-therapy patient test; mentioned in confidence notes only.

Goyal 2022 Open Forum Infect Dis and Goyal 2026 J Infect Dis: in-silico cohort analyses of response-guided shortening with no patient comparison of a shortened course; Gorstein 2020 Antiviral Res modelled sofosbuvir + ribavirin, no NS5A member drug.

Mawatari 2020 Hepatol Res (doi:10.1111/hepr.13474): one P32del patient among three glecaprevir/pibrentasvir retreatment failures; consistent with the TK-NOG mouse but pibrentasvir was not dosed in that model and the result was known in kind from Uemura 2019, so no prospective entry.
Chimpanzee, marmoset/GBV-B and primary-hepatocyte systems: no NS5A-class patient comparison found in the searches above; not added.

Japanese sofosbuvir/velpatasvir + ribavirin DAA-failure trial outcomes by P32del status: not verified within budget, so the TK-NOG forward prediction (velpatasvir regimens fail P32del) stays without a prospective entry.

Zitzmann 2026 CPT (bemnifosbuvir + ruzasvir, Perelson multiscale model fitted to NCT05904470 kinetics): a fit with no prediction compared with patients, on the existing hcv-viral-kinetic-model system; not added.

Kai 2015 J Gastroenterol (TK-NOG, DCV/ASV-failure serum, ledipasvir + GS-558093 failed EOT/SVR) vs Suda 2017 (LDV/SOF+RBV SVR 13/15), Kawakami 2017 (26/30), Ikeda 2018 (19/29): belongs on the existing hcv-tk-nog-humanized-liver-mouse track as a 2015 untested opener and a 2017 contra, but the merge appends after the draft's 2019 entries (lint: years not sorted), so it is left to a checker verdict on that track rather than added here.

gaps.lead: Shi 2013 humanized-mouse GT2 combination failure vs Sulkowski 2014 daclatasvir + sofosbuvir 92% SVR in GT2
gaps.detail: Changes nothing scored; rule question 2 already carries it. Shi 2013 abstract (PMID 23322441) gives the GT2a/2b failure for 4-week BMS-788329 + BMS-605339 (NS3 PI) or + BMS-821095 (NS5B non-nucleoside), and attributes it to the partners: 'Anti-HCV effects of BMS-605339 and BMS-821095 were more potent against genotype 1b than against genotype 2a.' Sulkowski 2014 (NEJM 370:211, PMID 24428467, NCT01359644) cured 92% of 26 GT2 patients with daclatasvir + sofosbuvir (nucleotide) for 24 weeks: neither the partner class nor the duration the mouse tested, so no admissible contra on hcv-chimeric-upa-scid-mouse; efficacy 3 stays retro. Only the judgement wording 'never tested with a member drug' is loose (unscored).

gaps.lead: FDA Harvoni label Oct 2014 section 12.4 baseline NS5A RAPs relapse 5/23 vs 2/85
gaps.detail: efficacy 4 (hcv-replicon-huh7, first patient-level entry): field year (with epub_year/print_year, src, srcLabel, quote), current 2015 / FDA Daklinza label 2015, source supports 2014 / FDA Harvoni label Oct 2014 section 12.4 (http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/205834s000lbl.pdf; bundle sources/205834/205834s000lbl.txt lines 1105-1127), which pairs ledipasvir replicon resistance positions with relapse: 'In treatment-experienced subjects whose virus had baseline NS5A polymorphisms at resistance-associated positions, relapse rates were 22% (5/23) after 12 weeks and 0% (0/19) after 24 weeks of treatment with HARVONI.' Status stays same (patient-level), but source_calls_it should be partial: in treatment-naive ION-1/ION-3 relapse was 6% (3/48) vs 5% (8/167) at 8 weeks and 1% vs 1% at 12 weeks with vs without baseline RAPs. The Daklinza 2015 Y93H/ALLY-3 comparison can remain as a strengthening note.

gaps.lead: Osawa 2019 GLE/PIB humanized mice and Doi 2019 P32del humanized-liver mice
gaps.detail: Doi 2019 is tracked as hcv-tk-nog-humanized-liver-mouse (efficacy 9-10); Osawa 2019 used the Hiroshima uPA/SCID system, a retrodiction belonging on hcv-chimeric-upa-scid-mouse (efficacy 3 track), needing a verdict entry there

gaps.lead: Kai (checker: Kan) 2015 TK-NOG DCV/ASV-failure prediction and 2017 LDV/SOF retreatment tests
gaps.detail: efficacy 9 (hcv-tk-nog-humanized-liver-mouse opener): year 2019 -> 2015, src Doi 2019 -> Kan 2015 (J Gastroenterol 50:1145, doi:10.1007/s00535-015-1108-6, PMID 26208695, epub 2015-07-25), model_first_use_year 2019 -> 2015; the checker verdict on efficacy 9 already proposes this part. Not proposed anywhere and not appendable in year order from models.json: a 2017 contra entry between the opener and efficacy 10 (2019 retro). Model side, Kan 2015 abstract: 'Administration of ledipasvir/GS-558093 (a NS5B nucleotide analog) in these mice failed to achieve end-of-treatment response or sustained virologic response' (DCV/ASV-failure virus, NS3 D168V + NS5A L31V + Y93H; prospective, product_in_model true, prediction_level patient). Patient side, Suda 2017 (J Gastroenterol 52:1122, doi:10.1007/s00535-017-1328-z, PMID 28315983, epub 2017-03-18; 13/15 carried NS5A L31 + Y93H): 'Overall, 86.7% (13/15) of patients achieved a sustained viral response, and all patients completed therapy.' Kawakami 2018 (doi:10.1007/s00535-017-1380-8, PMID 28815329, epub 2017-08-16): SVR12 26/30, failures linked to cirrhosis plus L31M/I + Y93H. Proposed: efficacy, year 2017, status contra, retrodiction false, comparison_stated false, source_tier 1, model_src Kan 2015 (tier 1), magnitude opposite, endpoint_role primary, confidence medium (abstract-level; patients got 12 weeks with ribavirin and sofosbuvir, mice ledipasvir + GS-558093 without ribavirin).
No publication with preclinical-to-patient data (PubMed 0 relevant, Europe PMC 0 relevant); 4 CT.gov trials with no posted results

Only comparison is replicon EC50/resistance (AAC 2014) vs single-dose and 28-day viral-load declines (Wilfret 2013, Gardner 2014): the existing hcv-replicon-huh7 system, so no new system (MODELS_TASK: skip systems the draft tracks)
Replicon potency (BMCL 2016) then STORM-C-1 and phase 2/3 SVR trials; no model beyond the existing hcv-replicon-huh7 system and no published model-to-patient comparison

Replicon/RAS profile (AAC 2018) is the existing hcv-replicon-huh7 system; Zitzmann 2026 multiscale model is a fit to patient kinetics on the existing hcv-viral-kinetic-model system with no prediction compared
